issues.explanation: B4 expresses existing SAFE principal as 34% of the $15M cap. That is a ratio of dollars to the cap, not an ownership share, and it can be misread as dilution. The Form C capitalization tables give the issuer's own fully diluted split (common 74.64%, SAFEs 25.36%, assuming conversion before this Offering). That is a better-sourced dilution figure and B omitted it. It is an issuer-stated figure, and its derivation is not shown. It does not include this Offering's SAFEs or the 1.5% intermediary securities.
issues.target: B4 / B3 / price_and_terms: dilution from existing SAFEs

issues.explanation: The $1,000,000 maximum is about 1.04x the FY2025 operating cash outflow of $960,595 (C13), before intermediary fees and the $5,000 onboarding fee. It is not 'small' against that figure. The target of $75,000 is small. The statement should say that only the target is small. At the maximum, gross proceeds roughly match one year of FY2025 outflow. Whether the maximum is reached is unknown.
issues.target: economics_and_funding: 'Even the maximum is small against the FY2025 cash burn'

issues.explanation: The A-stage input flags the existing SAFEs as 'conversion_terms_disclosed: true', but only the $15M cap is cited. The reviewed note says that for existing Crowd SAFEs the company 'may elect either to continue the instrument without conversion' on an Equity Financing (C4). This differs from the automatic conversion in this Offering's form. Discount, MFN and the actual existing-SAFE form are not in the pack. The flag should read partial. The existing SAFEs' share count cannot be derived from the pack.

Three documents describe priority differently: the SAFE form (junior to debt, on par with other SAFEs and preferred, senior to common), the Form C risk factor (payment only after creditors and more senior holders including preferred are paid in full), and the reviewed note (equal priority with common equity on dissolution) (C5). B recorded only the note conflict. The SAFE form is the operative text, but the conflict should be weighed. No waterfall or intercreditor terms are stated for the all-asset EIDL lien.

B5 says the amounts 'differ by date and Wayflyer status'. The pack shows more than that. The note table shows a Wayflyer balance of $31,795 at 2025-12-31 with maturity 02/28/2026. The Form C shows $51,000 outstanding with maturity February 28, 2027, and describes '1% per month' with 'Monthly payment of $1,989 per week'. The balance has risen and the maturity has moved. The note says no subsequent events needed disclosure through issuance (report dated 2026-07-23). Either a new advance or a modification happened and is undisclosed, or the Form C figure is wrong. Terms are internally inconsistent (monthly vs weekly). Request an explanation. This is not proof of misstatement.

B notes the cap is 32.7x FY2025 revenue (B12) but does not mention that the existing 2022 SAFEs carry the same $15,000,000 cap (C3). The cap therefore has not moved since 2022, while FY2024 and FY2025 revenue were $347,602 and $459,216. Investors from 2022 and this Offering share the cap but not necessarily other terms. This is a fact, not a verdict on price. No comparables are in the pack.

B6 found service-booking boilerplate in the receivables note. The Business section shows more of the same: 'institution integrations', 'institutional deployment' and 'white-label customer integration' (C6), plus risk factors on 'product candidates' (A28). These fit another business model. The 'lower confidence in care' reading is an analyst inference. It should be stated as such, with a request for corrected disclosure. It is not proof of misstatement. Execution risk item (4), which cites suppliers, co-packers and tariffs, has no claim ids. The risk-factor text is on p.17-19 and should be tied to claims.

B7 notes that the press release names vertical integration as 'a core use of proceeds' and that the Form C table lacks it. The Form C also says the issuer 'does not intend to make any material capital expenditures in the near future' (C7). Completing vertical integration would normally involve spend, and none is quantified. The two statements conflict, and the plan, cost and timing are undisclosed.
issues.target: B7 use of proceeds: vertical integration

issues.explanation: Critical item status is overstated. The pack's own checklist marks fees as missing, and A7 admits investor-side fees are not stated. Investors must open a custody account (C8). The custodial agreement's fee schedule is blank, says the Client pays fees, and sets payment terms. The SAFE says the Custody Account Agreement takes precedence over the SAFE where they conflict. The investor's cost of holding is therefore unknown. Also, the custodian name differs between documents (A35). Downgrade to partial.

B13 notes the press release (2026-09-24) precedes the Form C signature (2026-09-28). The same release says the campaign is 'now live' yet carries a disclaimer that 'No offer to buy or sell securities is being made' (C9). These are internally inconsistent. The Form C also warns some testing-the-waters communications 'may not have included proper disclaimers'. I do not find a violation; that is a legal question. It lowers the weight of the 'live' claim. Availability stays unverified.

The going-concern note counts only 'liquid assets in cash of $116,414'. The balance sheet also shows $1,397,792 in marketable securities, mostly municipal bonds (C10). B cites both but does not point out this tension in the reviewed note. The 2025 cash flow was funded in part by drawing down the portfolio. The $654,000 at 2026-06-30 is unreviewed. Its relation to the portfolio is unexplained. Read literally, the issuer's own '5 months' from 2026-06-30 ends before the 2026-12-18 deadline (C11). That is a reading of a stale issuer statement, not a computed current runway. No interim statements are provided.

Cost of goods sold per the note includes shipping, freight-out, fulfillment (Amazon, Shopify, Walmart) and warehousing (C12). The gross loss is therefore not a pure production margin. 'Unit economics not yet shown to be positive' is fair, but the gross loss cannot be tied to production cost. Vertical integration may not address fulfillment cost. Channel and SKU margins are missing.

A34 says the issuer may extend the deadline or raise the maximum, but the cited p.2 passage supports only the no-sale and refund rule. Extension and increase rights are on p.23. Partial support. Also, A13 'under no obligation to convert except on a qualified financing' relies on p.24 (cited in B9), not p.25.

A35 covers CEO control of amendments. It omits that disputes go to binding AAA arbitration seated within 15 miles of Wood-Ridge, NJ (C14). Together with a Lead who is the issuer's CEO and who both amends terms and votes as proxy, investor remedies are narrow. Enforceability and practical effect are legal questions beyond the pack.
issues.target: PC3 investor rights: dispute and amendment provisions

issues.explanation: B9 says this SAFE offering does not by itself trigger conversion. This is a plausible reading of the 'Equity Financing' definition, which excludes SAFEs and notes, and B flags it for counsel. Form C p.34 says the issuer may also raise capital via stock, SAFEs or notes from accredited investors outside this Offering. Only a priced round of at least $1,000,000 would convert this SAFE. Its timing and likelihood are not in the pack.
